body:
Some small notes that did not feel worth to open a separate issue.

---

> 6.3.4 Verify that users are notified of suspicious authentication attempts. This may include successful or unsuccessful authentication from an unusual location or client, partially successful authentication with only one of multiple factors, successful or unsuccessful authentication after a long period of inactivity or successful authentication after several unsuccessful attempts.


really hard to read.

---

> 6.3.7 Verify that a hardware-based authentication mechanism is supported that provides impersonation resistance against phishing attacks (such as WebAuthn) and verifies intent to authenticate by requiring a user-initiated action (such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key).

FIDO

---

> 6.4.4 Verify that if OTP or other multi-factor authentication factors are lost, that evidence of identity proofing is performed at the same level as during enrollment.

OTP

---

> 6.5.1 Verify that lookup secrets, out-of-band authentication requests or codes, and time-based, one-time passwords (TOTPs) are only usable once.

Maybe successfully used once? or are invalidated after successful use or expiration.

Otherwise one may read that you need to keep global list of already used codes.

---

> 6.5.8 Verify that time-based OTPs are checked based on a time source from a trusted service and not from an untrusted or client provided time.

OTPs

---

> 6.6.2 Verify that out-of-band authentication requests, codes, or tokens are only usable for the original authentication request for which they were generated and not a previous or subsequent one.

Maybe asking "binding to authentication request"?

---

> 6.6.3 Verify that a code based out-of-band authentication mechanism is protected against brute force attacks by using either rate limiting or a code with at least 64 bits of entropy.

and 

> 6.6.4	Verify that, where push notifications are used for multi-factor authentication, rate limiting or number matching is used to prevent push bombing attacks.


Rate limiting must be in place anyway...

comments.body:
I started here: #2899


> > 6.6.3 Verify that a code based out-of-band authentication mechanism is protected against brute force attacks by using either rate limiting or a code with at least 64 bits of entropy.
> 
> and
> 
> > 6.6.4	Verify that, where push notifications are used for multi-factor authentication, rate limiting or number matching is used to prevent push bombing attacks.
> 
> Rate limiting must be in place anyway...

I am not sure what you mean, are you saying that both are talking about rate limiting? If so, the first is rate limiting on entering codes and the second is rate limiting on push notifications.

Alternatively, do you meant that rate limiting is a separate requirement? If so, I think that we judged that these requirements are important enough to specifically mention it.

> brute force attacks by using either rate limiting or a code with at least 64 bits of entropy

If to read this, then it says use one OR another. Which means that if "code with at least 64 bits of entropy" then you don't need to use rate limiting? This is in a way in conflict with a separate requirement we have for rate limiting.

Not sure is it intentional or not, but acronyms were not addressed for requirements:
* 6.3.7 FIDO
* 6.5.8 OTPs

> Not sure is it intentional or not, but acronyms were not addressed for requirements:
> 
> * 6.3.7 FIDO
> * 6.5.8 OTPs

Is it not sufficient that we mention the acronym above and in the glossary?

> > brute force attacks by using either rate limiting or a code with at least 64 bits of entropy
> 
> If to read this, then it says use one OR another. Which means that if "code with at least 64 bits of entropy" then you don't need to use rate limiting? This is in a way in conflict with a separate requirement we have for rate limiting.

I think that is the beauty of specifically mentioning it here. Either you need to specifically think about it or it just gets covered by the regular rate limiting requirement.

> Is it not sufficient that we mention the acronym above and in the glossary?

It is required from the point of view that "the requirement text must be full and understandable out of the rest of the document."

> I think that is the beauty of specifically mentioning it here. Either you need to specifically think about it or it just gets covered by the regular rate limiting requirement.

If you want this kind of beauty, it should say: "Additionally to rate limiting it should be considered to use code with at least 64 bits of entropy". The usage of "OR" there is incorrect compared to requirements in "V2.4 Anti-automation"

> > Is it not sufficient that we mention the acronym above and in the glossary?
> 
> It is required from the point of view that "the requirement text must be full and understandable out of the rest of the document."

FIDO makes no real sense on its own so I don't think it adds value to expand it but I fixed OTP.

> > I think that is the beauty of specifically mentioning it here. Either you need to specifically think about it or it just gets covered by the regular rate limiting requirement.
> 
> If you want this kind of beauty, it should say: "Additionally to rate limiting it should be considered to use code with at least 64 bits of entropy". The usage of "OR" there is incorrect compared to requirements in "V2.4 Anti-automation"

See: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/pull/2899/commits/4636fdda40303e2026a801a49a5640b64052cdce
